running on the DEEPX **DX-M1 NPU**. Headings and tables are preserved.

This app is the documented **IFactory exception**: RapidDoc ships its own on-device NPU
pipeline, so instead of `dx_engine.InferenceEngine` + `SyncRunner`, the deliverable is
our **own standalone entry** (`pdf_to_markdown.py`) that imports the **vendored**
`rapid_doc` package (DEEPX fork, branch `rapid_doc_deepx`) and drives the pipeline.
Layout / OCR / table run on the NPU; formula recognition runs on ONNX Runtime (the fork
does not support formula on DX Engine).

## Quick start

```bash
./setup.sh                       # venv + deps + dx_engine bridge + NPU model download
./run.sh                         # parse the bundled sample_input.pdf (auto method)
./run.sh mydoc.pdf auto          # a digital PDF (text layer first, OCR fallback)
./run.sh scan.pdf  ocr           # a scanned PDF (force full OCR on the NPU)
./run.sh doc.pdf   txt           # text-layer extraction only (no OCR)
```

Outputs land under `output/<stem>/<parse-method>/`:

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `<stem>.md` | structured Markdown — headings, HTML `<table>`, formulas |
| `<stem>_content_list.json` | structured JSON content list (block-level) |
| `output/performance_summary.md` | per-stage NPU timings for the last run |

## `--parse-method`

| Method | Behavior | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| `auto` (default) | Use the PDF's embedded text layer per page; fall back to OCR where missing | digital or mixed PDFs — fastest, most accurate |
| `txt` | Text layer only, no OCR | known-digital PDFs |
| `ocr` | Force full OCR (det + rec) on every page on the NPU | scanned / image-only PDFs |

## Measured NPU performance

Hardware: **DX-M1** (`dxrt-cli -s`: M1, FW v2.5.6, runtime 3.3.2). Sample:
`sample_input.pdf` — a 9-page financial report with 9 tables and 21 headings.

### `auto` method (text layer + layout + table on NPU) — 12.63 s wall, 9 pages

| Pipeline Step | Count | Avg Latency | Throughput | Time (s) | Ratio |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Layout (NPU)   |  9 | 289.71 ms | 3.5 FPS  | 2.61 | 22.4% |
| PDF text-det   | 82 |   0.45 ms | 2232 FPS | 0.04 |  0.3% |
| Table (NPU)    | 13 | 692.97 ms | 1.4 FPS  | 9.01 | 77.3% |

Avg per page **1.29 s**. Model load: formula 1.02 s, ocr 0.54 s, layout 0.16 s, table 0.04 s.

### `ocr` method (full OCR det + rec on NPU) — 14.65 s wall, 9 pages

| Pipeline Step | Count | Avg Latency | Throughput | Time (s) | Ratio |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Layout (NPU)   |  9 | 374.81 ms | 2.7 FPS  | 3.37 | 17.4% |
| OCR det (NPU)  | 63 |  55.73 ms | 17.9 FPS | 3.51 | 18.1% |
| Table (NPU)    | 13 | 833.94 ms | 1.2 FPS  | 10.84 | 56.0% |
| OCR rec (NPU)  | 102 |  16.14 ms | 62.0 FPS | 1.65 |  8.5% |

Avg per page **2.15 s**. All four inference stages above run on the DX-M1 NPU.

> `sample_output.md` in this folder is the `auto`-method render of `sample_input.pdf`
> (21 headings, 9 HTML tables with full financial figures preserved).

## How it works

1. `pdf_to_markdown.py` puts the vendored `./rapid_doc` on `sys.path`, enforces
   closed-network mode (`MINERU_MODEL_SOURCE=local`), and checks the DX-RT threading env.
2. It builds the per-model engine configs (layout `PP-DocLayout-L`, OCR `PP-OCRv5`
   det+rec with ratio-based multi-model selection, table `UNET`, formula
   `PP-FormulaNet+ M`), pointing layout/OCR/table at the local `dxnn_models/` (NPU).
3. `rapid_doc … pipeline_analyze.doc_analyze(...)` runs the streaming pipeline on the NPU.
4. The middle-JSON is rendered to Markdown (`MakeMode.MM_MD`) and a JSON content list
   (`MakeMode.CONTENT_LIST`) via `FileBasedDataWriter`.
5. Per-stage timings are pulled from the pipeline's perf stats into `performance_summary.md`.

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `pdf_to_markdown.py` | **our** standalone entry over the vendored NPU pipeline |
| `setup.sh` | venv + `requirements.deepx.txt` + dx_engine `.pth` bridge + model download |
| `run.sh` | launcher: sources `set_env.sh`, `DXNN_DEVICES=0`, resolves abs input |
| `rapid_doc/` | vendored RapidDoc pipeline package (pure Python) |
| `deepx_scripts/`, `setup_sample_models.sh` | DX env setup + NPU/ONNX model downloader |
| `value_compare/recognition/character_dict_from_onnx.txt` | OCR recognition char dict |
| `sample_input.pdf` / `sample_output.md` | sample PDF and its rendered Markdown |
| `dxnn_models/`, `onnx_models/` | downloaded models (16 `.dxnn` NPU + 8 `.onnx`) |
| `session.log` | real captured output of the inference runs |

## Requirements

- DEEPX DX-M1 NPU with DX-RT 3.3.2 (`bash dx-runtime/scripts/sanity_check.sh --dx_rt` PASS).
- `dx_engine` is bridged from `dx-runtime/venv-dx-runtime` via a `.pth` written by `setup.sh`
  (no separate install). All other deps live in the self-contained session `venv/`.

107	
108	Each agent invocation MUST produce a **fresh** session directory whose name
109	starts with the current local timestamp. **Reusing a previous round's session
110	directory — even one created earlier today — is a HARD GATE violation** (see

MUST be the tee-captured stdout of real command execution — never a heredoc
template or programmatic write.

```bash
cat .current_dx_session_id           .current_dx_work_dir

```

```bash
# ✓ Correct — fresh timestamp from system clock
SESSION_ID="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)_<agent>_<coding_model>_<target_model>_<task>"
```

Even if a prior session-dir exists with the same model/task and looks
"complete", do not re-enter it. The harness expects each round to be an
